question: Does committing a rip-up only when its victims re-land (arm strict) or when the incomplete count strictly falls (arm count) leave fewer KiCad-unconnected items after pass 1 than Java's rip-up on at least N-1 eligible boards, with none worse, no new DRC errors and no via in a pad; and does it still win when both arms are followed by an Q10 sweep?
rule_text: each pair is judged by N02's totals rule (freerouting-dev gate --prereg on a records file per pair): hard metrics 0, guards not worse than the pair's baseline, no board worse than twice its band, and the summed signal improved by more than the set noise; pass_rule (the paired rule) is printed for each pair, not judged

mp1.engine: freerouting-rs release CLI of main at the run (amendment 1; one Linux build for every arm, its --version git sha in the note); the default profile

ripcost-5000.engine: freerouting-rs release CLI of main at the run (amendment 1; one Linux build for every arm, its --version git sha in the note); the default profile
ripcost-5000.what: Q11.1's sweep (amendment 1): pass 1 at start_ripup_costs 5000; the later flag wins over the 1500 of the base command

ripcost-20000.engine: freerouting-rs release CLI of main at the run (amendment 1; one Linux build for every arm, its --version git sha in the note); the default profile
ripcost-20000.what: Q11.1's sweep (amendment 1): pass 1 at start_ripup_costs 20000; the later flag wins over the 1500 of the base command

ripcost-near-off.engine: freerouting-rs release CLI of main at the run (amendment 1; one Linux build for every arm, its --version git sha in the note); the default profile
ripcost-near-off.what: Q11.1's sweep (amendment 1): pass 1 at start_ripup_costs 1000000 ('near-off': each item's rip cost is capped at i32::MAX/100, so rip-up is priced out, not switched off; operator decision 2026-10-18 in Q11.1); the later flag wins over the 1500 of the base command

ripcost-best.engine: freerouting-rs release CLI of main at the run (amendment 1; one Linux build for every arm, its --version git sha in the note); the default profile
ripcost-best.what: baseline: the Q11.1 arm (mp1 = 1500, ripcost-5000, ripcost-20000, ripcost-near-off) with the fewest kicad_unconnected summed over the eligible rows, ties by fewest vias; amendment 1: its records are that arm's runs (no run of its own), named in the amendment that writes `eligible`

strict.engine: freerouting-rs release CLI of main at the run (amendment 1; one Linux build for every arm, its --version git sha in the note); the default profile
strict.what: candidate: transaction, every victim net must re-land (Q11.2)

pairs_rule: amendment 1: the verdict pair is (mp1, strict), judged by the totals rule; (ripcost-best, strict) is judged the same way and strict passes only if it passes both; the Q11.1 arms are Q11.1's table, not judged. Registered: baseline_arm/candidate_arm name the primary pair for freerouting-dev gate; every pair is judged on its own by the totals rule; a candidate passes only if it passes against both mp1 and ripcost-best, and its +sweep arm is reported against mp1+sweep (the composed flow, Q00)

boards.eligibility: every board of tools/bench/sets/benchmark.txt, owner.txt and the 2-layer medium/hard rows of kicad-corpus.txt on which the unchanged engine at the registration commit (arm mp1) leaves at least one incomplete connection; the list goes into `eligible` below, as an amendment that changes nothing else, before any candidate arm runs. canary-pwr-9511d9a and pours1..3 count as one board (grouped, as in Q01.json).
boards.grouped: none since amendment 1 (one canary-pwr row, canary-pwr-9511d9a); registered: fixtures/canary-pwr/*.dsn are one board for pass_rule
boards.board_flags: none beyond the arm commands; the canary-pwr flags are in every command (start_ripup_costs 1500, min_trace_width_um 150), as Q10.json uses them
boards.why: Q10's universe and eligibility rule: Q10, Q11 and Q12 are measured as one family (Q00), so they share the boards

grading: tools/kicad-oracle/grade.sh where a .kicad_pcb exists (copper severities forced to error, input DRC subtracted, refill on); canary-pwr by canary-23 (ses_import.py, kicad-cli pcb drc --schematic-parity --refill-zones --severity-all, via_in_pad.py, inner_tracks.py)

metric_definitions.work_units: the run's maze work units (freerouting-dev bench record); a rolled-back attempt's work stays on the meter, so it is counted
metric_definitions.kicad_unconnected: KiCad's unconnected items after importing the session
metric_definitions.unrouted: the router's final unrouted count (its log)

extra_reported: rip-stats (router.special.diagnostics=rip-stats): rips, reroutes, re-land share per arm
the job log's 'Transactional rip-up' tally: transactions, committed, rolled back, retries routed, victim nets, re-landed, re-rips refused
keep_rule: amendment 1: keep strict as a setting (off by default, in no profile) only if it passes the totals rule against both mp1 and ripcost-best. Registered: keep the best passing candidate as a setting (off by default, in no profile) only if it passes the totals rule against both mp1 and ripcost-best; with several passing, the fewest kicad_unconnected summed over the eligible boards, ties by fewest vias. A change to profile enhanced needs its own registration
stop_rule: one registered run per arm per board after P04's default-tree decision; no reruns with other settings, rules, depths or factors
not_registered: rule strict with depth 1 (built and tested, not an arm)
amendment 1: the arms count, depth1 and strict+ripfactor and every +sweep arm (dropped: two arms where the question allows)

decision_table.pass: keep the best passing arm as a setting (off by default); DIVERGENCES line
decision_table.fail: remove quality/transaction.rs and the ripup_factor hook; Q11.1's table and the numbers stay in Q11.6's done note

timing: measured only after P04's default-tree decision

amendments.after: the registration; before any registered run of any arm on any row (the done notes' spot checks on canary-pwr-9511d9a are not runs of this registration)
amendments.reason: decided 2026-10-20: measurement runs stay a few minutes: every row routes in well under a minute except canary-pwr's DSN, two arms where the question allows, one KiCad grade per distinct session. The registered 12 arms on 30 rows (each also with Q11.1's 4 sweep arms) would take hours
amendments.changes: (1) Rows: boards.files keeps the 15 rows of tools/bench/sets/q10-sweep-quick.txt, with each row's longest recorded route time and the target/orchestrator/<dir>/ it came from in that file: 8 benchmark boards at most 23.3 s, canary-pwr-9511d9a (pass 1 43.2 to 44.2 s, n06-i, n06-u; the only canary-pwr row, so no grouping) and 6 corpus rows at most 18.9 s; dropped for their route time: bm01 49.3 s, CPU-85 61.7 s, z10_module 200.9 s, smoothieboard 226.2 s, LogicBoard_smt 434.7 s, GP8B 500.4 s, coldfire 550.4 s, contribution-board 702.4 s, canary-pwr-pours1/2/3, -pours-as-planes and -2026-10-15-1747-unpoured (104 to 357 s), eprom-card-80bus 86.2 s and rio-iceshield 31.0 s. The eligibility rule (arm mp1 leaves at least one incomplete connection; `eligible` written by an amendment before any candidate run) and min_boards 3 are unchanged. (2) Arms: mp1, Q11.1's three sweep arms ripcost-5000, ripcost-20000 and ripcost-near-off (start_ripup_costs 1000000, Q11.1's operator decision of 2026-10-18), ripcost-best (the best Q11.1 arm's runs, no run of its own) and strict; count, depth1, strict+ripfactor and every +sweep arm are dropped, so the question's second half (with Q10's sweep after both arms) is not measured. Every command gains --router.special.diagnostics=rip-stats (report-only, it changes no route: the field's help in settings/fields.rs) so that Q11.1's table has its rip stats from the same runs; the engine is one release build of main at the run (P04's default-tree decision, Java's tree, is made, so the timing clause holds). (3) Grading: one KiCad grade per distinct session (two arms with byte-identical sessions on a row share one grade); the 8 benchmark rows have no .kicad_pcb and use the router's unrouted count (the signal's second name). (4) Every route runs under ulimit -v 8000000 with timeout 600 for canary-pwr-9511d9a and timeout 120 for the other rows; a timeout leaves the measurement incomplete. Nothing else changes: question's first half, metrics, totals block, stop_rule

amendments.after: amendment 1; before any registered run of any arm on any row
amendments.reason: the run's engine, runner and grading made precise before any number (amendment 1 names 'main at the run' and the grade scripts, not the metric sources), with the hard-guard reading every measurement since N06.4 uses
amendments.changes: (1) Engine: amendment 1's 'main at the run' is main 3330f36 (freerouting --version: git 3330f369a2ab), one Linux release build of freerouting-cli and freerouting-dev from a detached worktree of that commit (CLI sha256 a6bc2d82eceaf406...), default profile enhanced, every arm. (2) Runner: tools/bench/quick-arm.sh, which adds --result-json (the result manifest) to each route, and every route also gets --stats json (output only: the per-stage counters next to the SES, for work_units); outputs in target/orchestrator/q1112/out/<arm>/<board>.*. (3) Grading made precise: canary-pwr-9511d9a through Q10's canary grade (target/orchestrator/q10/s104/canary-grade.sh with its WSL kicad-cli shim, canary 9511d9a3: ses_import.py, kicad-cli pcb drc --schematic-parity --refill-zones --severity-all, via_in_pad.py, inner_tracks.py): kicad_unconnected = unconnected items, drc_real = error items other than unconnected items and starved thermals, below_minimum_raw = track_width errors, via_in_pad_raw = via_in_pad.py's count; the corpus rows through tools/kicad-oracle/grade.sh on target/corpus/projects/<id> with the engine `cp <session> {SES}` (tools/bench/grade-distinct.sh): kicad_unconnected = unconnected_items, drc_real = drc_real, below_minimum_raw = the sum of copper.below_minimum; the benchmark rows: kicad_unconnected and drc_real null (a null pair is not compared), below_minimum_raw = the session's traces narrower than the board's narrowest class width that the input does not have. On the benchmark and corpus rows via_in_pad_raw = added vias in SMD pads (main 4885a30's added_via_in_pad). Hard guards via_in_pad and below_minimum are 'no new breach versus baseline' (decided 2026-10-18: no registration carries a hard guard the baseline already breaks; the commands' 150 um floor with enhanced's neck-down breaks the raw KiCad track_width minimum in every arm, Q10.4): the arm's raw count minus the pair's baseline arm's raw count on the same row, floored at 0, so one records file per pair as rule_text says; the raw counts are reported in the done note. On every row: pour_lost_pins = quality::pour_audit::audit (input board against input + SES), vias and length_mm = the imported session's statistics, all three by a scratch tool on the engine API at the same commit (N06.13's n06m plus Q10's pour audit, target/orchestrator/q1112/q11m); unrouted = the result manifest's board_statistics.connections.incomplete_count (the log's final unrouted count) and connections = its maximum_count (the default noise band of rows without a registered band); work_units = maze_work_units of the --stats total; wall_seconds = /usr/bin/time's elapsed seconds (other sessions' routes and builds ran at the same time: reported, not compared). (4) Numbering: the `eligible` amendment that amendment 1's notes call amendment 2 is amendment 3. Written before any registered run of any arm on any row. Nothing else changes: arms, commands, rows, metrics, totals block, pairs, keep and stop rules

amendments.after: mp1's registered runs; before any candidate arm runs
amendments.reason: the registration's eligibility rule: `eligible` is written as an amendment before any candidate arm runs, and Q11.1 names ripcost-best
amendments.changes: eligible: the 11 rows on which mp1 (main 3330f36, amendment 2) left at least one incomplete connection, 11 distinct boards (all but Issue649-kicad_ecc83-pp_input_board_v1, Issue508-DAC2020_bm02, Issue508-DAC2020_bm07 and mccx11-hardware-sx1262-433mhz-reverse-engineering, complete under mp1); the verdicts are read on these rows (freerouting-dev gate --eligible), every registered row is still run and recorded. Written after mp1's runs (and Q11.1's sweep arms, which are not candidates) and before any candidate arm runs. ripcost-best is ripcost-5000 (start_ripup_costs 5000): kicad_unconnected summed over the six graded eligible rows is 185 for mp1, 172 for ripcost-5000, 175 for ripcost-20000 and 175 for ripcost-near-off; its records are ripcost-5000's runs (amendment 1), and its command and settings now name 5000 in place of {Q11.1}. Nothing else changes
